MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Record keeping in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Record keeping in aquaculture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Record keeping in aquaculture.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Record keeping in aquaculture.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Fish culture? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Fish culture.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Fish culture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Fish culture.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conservation of marine and freshwater environments? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.

9. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Reproduction.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Reproduction.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Reproduction.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Safety of Humans and Equipment Undertaking Marine Activities and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Marine Resource Utilisation 4.4 Blue Economy and Marine Entrepreneurship Page 12 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Marine Resource Utilisation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Blue Economy and Marine Entrepreneurship Page 12 of 51 STRAND 1.0: FISH BIOLOGY  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. C — Ice melting to water

3. B — 100 °C

4. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

5. D — Glucose and oxygen

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.

9. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.

11. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Marine Resource Utilisation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
